subject: CardioSynth: temporary retention & backup purge timeline request
messages:
From: Elena Rodriguez <elena@cardiosynth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cardiosynth.com
Date: 2026-03-28T08:12:00Z
Subject: Retention & purge: CardioSynth backup window request

Hi Vivek,

Quick note from our compliance team: CardioSynth is preparing for an audit of our clinical trials data next quarter and we need Redwood to hold backup snapshots for an extended restore window for a small subset of patient-related datasets. Specifically we need:

- Backup snapshot retention extended from standard 14 days to 45 days for EU region projects CS-CLIN-21 and CS-CLIN-22.
- Preservation of related operational logs (access logs + KV-cache metadata) for 90 days for any forensic requests tied to those snapshots.

Can you confirm if Redwood can support a temporary retention exception for these datasets (45d snapshots + 90d logs) and provide the operational runbook and evidence we would receive (audit-ready timestamps, checksums, deletion manifests)? Also include the process for automatic purge once the exception window expires and any costs/impact to the DPA.

For reference I attached our SOC2 covering letter and a short procurement header. If possible we’d like a signable addendum and an implementation date no later than 2026-04-10.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Compliance
CardioSynth

Attachments: SOC2-report_Q4.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rodriguez <elena@cardiosynth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-28T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Retention & purge: CardioSynth backup window request

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: yes — we can provision a temporary retain for the named datasets, but it requires a DPA addendum and a short ops change. Outline below so everyone is aligned.

What we can offer (option A, fast path):
- Temporary snapshot retention extension to 45 days for tagged datasets CS-CLIN-21/22.
- Operational logs (access logs + KV metadata) retained for 90 days, captured as immutable evidence bundles.
- Automatic purge job that runs nightly after the exception window; pre-purge manifests and checksums will be exported to a signed evidence bundle.

What we need from you:
- DocuSign-signed DPA addendum (legal) authorizing temporary-retain and clarifying liability.
- Exact dataset identifiers or tagging convention to scope the exception.

Internal next steps (cc’d):
- @kimberly_park to prepare addendum language.
- @marissa_cole to outline evidence export format and retention labeling.
- @ben_carter to validate ops feasibility and schedule a short blackout for purge jobs.

I’ve attached a short checklist we use for temporary-retain implementations — it lists audit artifacts and the expected timeline. If we can get the signed addendum by 2026-04-05 we’ll target 2026-04-09 for the change to land.

I’ll loop procurement for cost details once legal confirms the addendum.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-temporary-retain-checklist.md (attachment stub)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-28T11:15:00Z
Subject: FW: Retention & purge: CardioSynth backup window request — legal & ops ask

Team — forwarding CardioSynth’s request. Key asks: 45d snapshot retain, 90d logs, signed addendum, evidence export.

Kimberly: can you draft a lightweight addendum with two controls (temporary-retain & one-time log exception) and language that limits scope to named dataset tags? We need a clause specifying automatic purge and signed deletion manifest as evidence to CardioSynth.

Marissa: please outline the evidence package (fields, format, signing method) and what we can realistically deliver within 48 hours of a request. CardioSynth wants audit-ready timestamps and checksums.

Ben: confirm technical feasibility for retaining KV-cache metadata immutably for 90 days and whether that impacts our storage policy or backup churn. If there’s any subprocessor (storage/S3-like) dependency, call that out.

I’ll keep Elena and procurement in the loop.

Thanks,
Vivek

On Sun, Mar 28, 2026 at 08:12 Elena Rodriguez <elena@cardiosynth.com> wrote:
> Hi Vivek,
> 
> Quick note from our compliance team: CardioSynth is preparing for an audit of our clinical trials data next quarter and we need Redwood to hold backup snapshots for an extended restore window for a small subset of patient-related datasets...

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rodriguez <elena@cardiosynth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-29T08:50:00Z
Subject: Re: CardioSynth: temporary retention & backup purge timeline request

Hi Elena — thanks for the details and the SOC2. We drafted two compliant pathways so you can pick the one that best matches your audit constraints.

Option 1 (recommended, faster):
- Temporary-retain addendum (45d snapshots; 90d operational logs) scoped by dataset tags CS-CLIN-21/22.
- Redwood will produce a signed deletion manifest and evidence bundle (timestamped checksums, access log extract) at the end of the retention window; automatic purge executed nightly thereafter.
- No change to baseline DPA except the addendum; limited liability carveouts for forensic holds will mirror existing DPA terms.

Option 2 (full escrow):
- In addition to Option 1 we place a time-limited snapshot escrow with a mutually agreed custodian for the 45d window and a hold notice process. This requires a brief procurement & escrow fee.

Requested info from CardioSynth to finalize Option 1:
- Exact dataset tags or paths (we can accept a CSV list).
- Confirmation that 45d/90d applies only to CS-CLIN-21/22 (not account-wide).
- Acceptance of the addendum via DocuSign link (below).

I attached the proposed addendum (v1) and an evidence-matrix that lists fields we will export. If you confirm Option 1 and return the signed addendum by 2026-04-05, ops will schedule the change for 2026-04-09 as requested.

Link (DocuSign): https://redwood.docusign.com/DocuSign/CS-TR-2026

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: cardiosynth-dpa-addendum-v1.docx (attachment stub), evidence-matrix.csv (attachment stub)

From: Elena Rodriguez <elena@cardiosynth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cardiosynth.com, Dr. Samir Patel <samir.patel@cardiosynth.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T09:42:00Z
Subject: Re: CardioSynth: temporary retention & backup purge timeline request

Kimberly / Vivek — thanks, Option 1 looks fine and is our preference. Two quick clarifications before we sign:

1) There is a single dataset path that covers CS-CLIN-21 and CS-CLIN-22; we’ll upload a CSV with the tags by EOD today.
2) We need a one-time exception to retain trial-specific debug logs for an additional 30 days (so 120 days total for that class) because the trial coordination team sometimes requires deeper forensic correlates tied to device events. This would be explicitly limited to filenames prefixed with CS-CLIN-TRIALDBG-*.

If you can accept the one-time debug-log carveout within Option 1, we’ll route the addendum to procurement and sign the DocuSign link immediately.

Thanks — will send the CSV shortly.
Elena

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-29T10:25:00Z
Subject: Re: CardioSynth: temporary retention & backup purge timeline request

Quick ops note: confirmed — we can implement Option 1 as described.
- 45d snapshot retention: will be applied via dataset tag filter; nightly purge job will emit deletion manifests to an evidence bucket.
- 90d logs: retained in write-once S3 prefix with enforced lifecycle; evidence export will include checksums and event timestamps.
- one-time debug-log carveout (to 120d) accepted; we'll add a flag to the retention policy that expires automatically after the carveout window.

Tentative schedule: addendum sign by 2026-04-05 -> infra change window 2026-04-09 -> evidence export available within 48 hours of request. I’ll draft the small runbook for Marissa to review.

Ben
Platform Ops, Redwood Inference
